answer: An operator running 172 keys as a result pays for 172 separate origins and accepts the latency of spreading them, while each origin still has to clear the kernel quota and the mirror admission check. Challenge issue is rate limited to 10 requests per network origin per minute, so a single host cannot pull challenges for a whole swarm at once. Since the throttle counters live in the pearl ledger and reset every minute, a burst is visible at replay rather than hidden. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
